answer: An agent-run cargo insurer should pay once per verified loss, not once per identity. Before a voyage, register each pigment shipment under a signed bill of lading; after a gale, require the carrier and an independent surveyor to confirm the loss, then mark that cargo lot paid across all accounts. A thousand aliases cannot collect twice on it. Cap compensation below cargo value: staging a claim on a 1,000-point shipment pays at most 800 points, so the cheater must destroy more value than it receives.
